# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **“apply the correct Manhattan/tie-to-8
rule, but use only the first three seed cells in row-major order and ignore all
later seeds.”** Every one of the five canonical pairs has exactly three seeds,
so this shortcut is answer-equivalent on all canonical demonstrations. The
source-bound lesson census confirms `ignore_after_first_three` fits 5/5
canonical pairs.

An exact disagreement input is retained at
`checks/question-shortcut/input.json` (generator seed `73001`, sample index `1`,
medium; validator errors `[]`):

```text
0000000000
0000000002
0000000000
0000000000
0000070000
0000300000
0000000009
0000000000
0000000000
0000000000
```

The fourth row-major seed is color 9 at `(6,9)`. The intended rule gives color
9 at `(4,9)`, while the three-seed shortcut gives color 2 there. Across the
whole grid they disagree at 15 cells; the exact coordinates and both values are
in `checks/question-shortcut/differences.json`.

I checked the intended output with the supported canonical Racket command:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply e438ce3e02ce \
  --input ../checks/question-shortcut/input.json \
  --out ../checks/question-shortcut/racket.json
```

from the packet root. It exited 0, executed rule hash `866bf2f14b22`, and bound
the final generator hash
`60a2cee1c491a112a7d37e67336131257da46cdb417cc03b92fc6c176a068c7f`.
The rival output was computed independently by
`generators/e438ce3e02ce/workspace/voronoi_probe.py` with
`limit_seeds=3` and is retained at `checks/question-shortcut/rival.json`.

The repaired generator deliberately emits such cases. Slots 1 and 5 of the
eight-slot schedule contain four consequential seeds, and slots 3 and 7 contain
five. Every seed must uniquely own at least one blank cell, so an added seed is
never decorative. In the 300-lesson production census, this shortcut was
refuted in 100/100 easy, 100/100 medium, and 100/100 hard lessons.
